photo.caption: Area of the Fertile Crescent, circa 9500 BP, with main sites. ʿAin Ghazal is one of the important sites of the Pre-Pottery Neolithic period. The area of Mesopotamia proper was not yet settled by humans.
photo.description: Map of Southwest Asia showing the main archaeological sites of the Pre-Pottery Neolithic period, BCE c. 7500, in the "Fertile Crescent". Black squares indicate pre-agricultural sites.

photo.caption: Ain Ghazal Statues: closeup of one of the bicephalous statues, c. 7000 BC (9,000 years ago)
photo.description: The statues of Ain Ghazal, at the Archaeological Museum of Jordan (Amman Citadel).
